fx_note: Approximate exchange rates (1 EUR in local currency), only used to convert caps and thresholds in the comparison tool.

locations.name: United Kingdom

film_uplift.label: Independent Film Tax Credit (53%, 39.75% net) for films with a core budget up to £15m

locations.min_spend: At least 10% of core spend in the UK; high-end TV at least £1m per broadcast hour
locations.cap_label: No cap; qualifying spend limited to 80% of core expenditure
locations.funding_note: Statutory credit, no annual budget
locations.paid: After the corporation tax return
locations.notes: The credit is taxable, so 34% is worth 25.5% net. 39% for animation, children's TV and UK VFX work (VFX is exempt from the 80% cap). 53% for independent films with a budget up to £15m. The old film and HETV reliefs close on 1 April 2027.

locations.name: Ireland

film_uplift.label: Scéal uplift (40%) for feature films with a budget under €20m and an Irish or EEA key creative

locations.min_spend: €125k eligible spend and €250k total production cost
locations.funding_note: Payable credit, no annual budget; up to 90% can be claimed in advance
locations.paid: Up to 90% in advance, balance on completion
locations.notes: Credit is paid untaxed. 40% for feature films under €20m (Scéal) and 40% on the first €10m when at least €1m is spent on Irish VFX. Cast and crew of any nationality qualify when working in Ireland. Runs to end 2028.

locations.name: Netherlands
locations.min_spend: Feature: €1m total cost and €150k Dutch spend; series: minimum budget per broadcast minute

cap.label: €3m per project and per company per year

locations.funding_note: Competitive rounds, ranked on points (€20m for film and €9.5m for high-end series in 2026)
locations.paid: 30% on signing, balance after audit
locations.notes: Selective: applications are ranked, so a strong project can still miss out when a round is oversubscribed. A Dutch producer or co-producer is required. International co-productions are served first in 2026. Next film deadline: 26 October 2026.

locations.name: Belgium
locations.assumption: No statutory rate: 38% is the typical net benefit of investor financing after the investor return and fees
locations.min_spend: No statutory minimum; tax shelter money limited to 50% of the budget
locations.funding_note: Depends on investor appetite via intermediaries, no state budget
locations.paid: Up front: it is financing, not a rebate
locations.notes: Not a rebate but private financing with a tax break for the investor. The producer's net benefit is typically 38 to 40% of eligible Belgian spend. Money arrives before the shoot. Requires a Belgian (co-)producer and a European work.

locations.name: Germany
locations.min_spend: DFFF I: €1m total cost and 25% German spend; DFFF II: €20m budget and €8m German spend; GMPF series: €30k per minute

cap.label: €5m (DFFF I) to €25m (DFFF II) per project; series up to €20m per season

locations.funding_note: First come, first served (€250m a year from 2026); intake for 2026 shoots closed in August 2026
locations.paid: In instalments during production
locations.notes: 30% since February 2025 across all three schemes. The pot runs out: as of August 2026 no more applications are accepted for shoots starting in 2026; the 2027 window opens in November 2026. Public aid is capped at 50% of the total cost.

locations.name: France
locations.scheme: Tax Rebate for International Production (TRIP / C2I)
locations.min_spend: €250k French spend and 5 shooting days in France
locations.funding_note: Statutory credit, no annual budget
locations.paid: After the fiscal year, via the French line producer
locations.notes: 40% when at least 15% of the shots are digitally treated and French VFX spend exceeds €2m. Pay of non-European performers now qualifies (capped at 30% of the budget). Extended to end 2028.

locations.name: Spain (mainland)
locations.min_spend: €1m Spanish spend (€200k for animation and post)
locations.funding_note: Statutory deduction, no annual budget
locations.paid: Through the tax position of a Spanish service company
locations.notes: 30% on the first €1m of Spanish spend, 25% above that. Claimed by an ICAA-registered Spanish service company and passed on through the service contract. Regional schemes go higher: Navarre 35%, Bizkaia up to 60%.

locations.name: Canary Islands (Spain)
locations.min_spend: €1m Canary Islands spend (€200k for animation and post)
locations.funding_note: Statutory deduction, no annual budget
locations.paid: Through the tax position of a Canary Islands service company
locations.notes: 50% on the first €1m, 45% above that (54% on the first €1m when Canary spend exceeds €1.8m). Requires a production or service company resident in the Canary Islands and a regional certificate.

locations.name: Italy
locations.min_spend: €250k Italian spend

cap.label: €20m per company per year (2024 rules; the 2026 reform introduced further caps)

locations.funding_note: Closed annual budget since 2026 (€100m for international productions)
locations.paid: Offset against Italian tax or sold to a bank at a 5 to 15% discount
locations.notes: Transferable credit granted to the Italian executive producer. The July 2026 reform kept 40% for international productions but moved to a closed annual budget, excluded AI-related costs and tightened documentation. Above-the-line costs of non-EEA persons qualify at 30%.

locations.name: Portugal
locations.min_spend: €500k eligible spend (medium track), €2.5m (large track)
locations.funding_note: First come, first served; €50m a year for 2026 to 2029
locations.paid: In stages during production
locations.notes: New scheme since June 2026, replacing the old cash rebate. Large track: 30% on the first €2m, 25% above. 40% in the interior, Madeira and the Azores. Cultural test and a local executive producer required.

locations.name: Malta
locations.assumption: Assumes the full 40%: 30% base, 35% with Maltese content or Malta Film Studios, 40% when local crew targets are met
locations.min_spend: €100k Malta spend and a budget above €200k
locations.cap_label: No per-project cap; above-the-line costs capped
locations.funding_note: No published annual budget
locations.paid: 10% advance, balance after final audit
locations.notes: 30% base, 35% when Malta plays Malta or Malta Film Studios are used, 40% when local crew and department targets are met. Crew of any nationality qualifies. Scheme valid to October 2028.

locations.name: Hungary
locations.min_spend: No published minimum; cultural test
locations.cap_label: No per-project cap; annual envelope HUF 70bn (2026)
locations.funding_note: Annual envelope; registration reopened without limits on 1 July 2026 after a pause, with a backlog
locations.paid: After audit, in HUF
locations.notes: Non-Hungarian costs may make up to 25% of the eligible spend, which lifts the effective rebate to 37.5% of Hungarian spend. Principal photography must start within 6 months of registration. Paid in forint, so budget the currency risk.

locations.name: Czech Republic
locations.min_spend: CZK 18m per feature, CZK 7.5m per series episode
locations.funding_note: Annual budget; new intake halted in March 2026 and reopens 1 September 2026
locations.paid: After settlement, in CZK; can take up to 2 years
locations.notes: 25% since 2025 (up from 20%), 35% for animation and VFX-only projects, plus 66% of the withholding tax paid by foreign cast and crew. Payment may be delayed up to two years under the 2026 rules.

locations.name: Poland
locations.min_spend: 75% of the financing secured at application; cultural test

cap.label: PLN 15m per production, PLN 20m per beneficiary per year

locations.funding_note: First come, first served until the annual pot is used
locations.paid: After completion, in PLN
locations.notes: Rolling applications until the annual budget is exhausted, with at least 10% reserved for animation. Requires a Polish producer, co-producer or service company.

locations.name: Iceland

spend_uplift.label: 35% when Icelandic spend is at least ISK 350m with at least 30 working days and 50 crew in Iceland

locations.min_spend: None
locations.funding_note: Open-ended, no annual budget
locations.paid: After completion and audit, in ISK
locations.notes: 35% when the production spends at least ISK 350m in Iceland over 30+ working days with 50+ crew. If more than 80% of the total cost is incurred in Iceland, costs elsewhere in the EEA also qualify. Extended to end 2028.

locations.name: Norway
locations.assumption: Assumes the project is selected; only five projects were funded in 2026
locations.min_spend: NOK 25m feature budget or NOK 10m per series episode; at least NOK 4m Norwegian spend and 30% non-Norwegian financing
locations.cap_label: Set per project by the annual award (NOK 84.7m for five projects in 2026)
locations.funding_note: One competitive round a year, heavily oversubscribed
locations.paid: After completion, in NOK
locations.notes: Ranked selection against a small annual envelope: 18 applicants asked for NOK 288m in 2026 and five were funded. Parliament has asked for a more competitive scheme from 2027.

locations.name: Canada: Ontario
locations.scheme: Ontario Production Services Tax Credit (OPSTC) + federal PSTC
locations.min_spend: C$1m total cost; series C$100k to C$200k per episode; Ontario labour at least 25% of the claimed spend
locations.funding_note: Refundable credits, no annual budget
locations.paid: With the corporate tax return, typically 12 to 18 months after spend
locations.notes: 21.5% on all qualifying Ontario spend (labour, services, tangible property), plus the federal 16% credit on Canadian labour only. Refundable, no cultural test; needs a permanent establishment in Ontario. The industry asked for 25% in 2026; not adopted so far.

locations.name: Canada: British Columbia
locations.scheme: BC Production Services Tax Credit + federal PSTC
locations.min_spend: C$1m total cost; series C$100k to C$200k per episode
locations.funding_note: Refundable credits, no annual budget
locations.paid: With the corporate tax return, typically 12 to 18 months after spend
locations.notes: Labour-only: 36% of qualifying BC labour (since 2025) plus the federal 16%, with uplifts of 6% regional, 6% distant location and 16% for animation and VFX labour. No cultural test; permanent establishment in BC required. Since 2026 no pre-certification, and 36 months to claim.

locations.name: Canada: Quebec
locations.scheme: Quebec film production services tax credit + federal PSTC
locations.min_spend: C$250k minimum budget
locations.funding_note: Refundable credits, no annual budget
locations.paid: With the corporate tax return, typically 12 to 18 months after spend
locations.notes: 25% on qualifying Quebec labour and property (raised from 20% in 2025), plus 16% on animation and VFX labour and the federal 16% on Canadian labour. Key creatives only count when they are Quebec residents. No cultural test.

locations.name: United States: Georgia
locations.assumption: Transferable, not refundable: the credit is sold to Georgia taxpayers at a discount, which is not deducted here
locations.min_spend: US$500k qualified Georgia spend per tax year
locations.funding_note: No annual budget and no sunset
locations.paid: Sold to Georgia taxpayers via brokers after a mandatory audit
locations.notes: 20% base plus 10% for the Georgia logo or approved promotion. Transferable credit: most productions sell it at a discount. Mandatory audit; no cultural test; no local entity required. Definitions modernised from 1 January 2026 (streaming covered).

locations.name: United States: New Mexico
locations.scheme: New Mexico Film Production Tax Credit
locations.min_spend: None
locations.cap_label: No per-project cap; annual aggregate US$150m (FY2027), excess queues to later years
locations.funding_note: Annual aggregate cap; claims beyond it are paid in later years
locations.paid: Refund after the tax filing
locations.notes: 25% base, plus 5% for TV series, 10% for shooting 60+ miles from Albuquerque or Santa Fe and 5% for using a qualified production facility, up to 40% in total. Non-resident crew qualifies at 15%. Refundable; audit above US$5m.

locations.name: United States: California
locations.scheme: California Film & TV Tax Credit Program 4.0
locations.assumption: Applies to below-the-line spend only; cast, director, writers and producers do not qualify
locations.min_spend: US$1m budget (features) or US$1m per episode

cap.label: Credit on the first US$120m of qualified spend per feature (US$20m for independents)

locations.funding_note: US$750m a year through June 2030, competitive ranking in fixed application windows
locations.paid: Against California tax; refundable election pays 90% over five years
locations.notes: Expanded in July 2025 from 20 to 25% to 35% (40% for a series relocating to California), with uplifts for shooting outside the Los Angeles zone, VFX and local hire. Competitive: projects are ranked on a jobs ratio within a US$750m annual pot.

locations.name: United States: New York
locations.scheme: New York State Film Production Credit
locations.min_spend: US$1m budget in the New York City area, US$250k elsewhere; 75% of stage work in New York
locations.cap_label: No per-project cap; above-the-line limited to 40% of other qualified costs
locations.funding_note: US$800m a year through 2036 (plus US$100m for independent films)
locations.paid: Refundable, in one tax year since 2025
locations.notes: 30% base, plus 10% for shooting mainly upstate and 5 to 10% Production Plus for repeat spenders. Above-the-line costs now qualify within limits. Apply before principal photography.

locations.name: Australia
locations.min_spend: A$20m qualifying Australian spend; series also A$1.5m per hour (PDV Offset: A$500k)
locations.funding_note: Refundable offset, no annual budget; state incentives stack on top
locations.paid: Through the company tax return after completion, no payments during production
locations.notes: 30% of all qualifying Australian production expenditure, including post and VFX; the separate PDV Offset gives 30% on post-only work. Requires an Australian company or permanent establishment and a training or workforce contribution. State incentives (NSW, Victoria, Queensland) can be added.

locations.name: New Zealand

spend_uplift.label: 5% uplift via a points test for productions spending at least NZ$20m in New Zealand

locations.min_spend: NZ$4m qualifying New Zealand spend (PDV: NZ$250k)
locations.funding_note: Government appropriation, not competitive
locations.paid: After completion; interim payments once spend passes NZ$50m
locations.notes: 20% cash grant on all qualifying spend including above-the-line, plus a 5% uplift for productions spending NZ$20m or more that score on the economic-benefit points test. Entry threshold dropped to NZ$4m on 1 January 2026. Needs a New Zealand SPV.

locations.name: South Africa
locations.scheme: DTIC Foreign Film and Television Production Incentive
locations.min_spend: R15m qualifying South African spend; at least 50% of principal photography and 21 shoot days in South Africa
locations.funding_note: Annual allocation with a payment backlog; adjudication resumed in August 2026
locations.paid: After an audited claim, subject to fund availability
locations.notes: 25% cash rebate plus a 5% uplift under conditions (majority black-owned service company or local post). The R25m cap makes the effective rate fall quickly on larger budgets. Payments have been delayed since 2025; a guideline review is under way, so verify the current status before you rely on it.

labour_note: Share of local spend assumed to be local labour, for schemes that only credit labour (Canada). Adjustable.
